doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: Odd Fellows and Masons drilling ranks
summary: Martin and Tom talk about the Odd Fellows parade and its drilling rank, led by Sam Nanny and George DeVoe, with Shepard Smith as head drillman, and the women's drill team of Miss Patterson that Tom played for.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: No, no, the mason parade over there. They had them on the other side too. Alright, now you take the odd fella parade over there, you take your best drilling rank. Old man Sam Nanny. No, that's right. Yeah, old man Sam Nanny, well he's in the drilling rank. Now you take... Oh, what he... Man, he was the head of it. George DeVoe.
They had all them... They used to parade when I was a kid.
So now I thought you used to come over here and make the character number over here. No, no, them people was over there.

All fellas parade over there. They all joined together, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. You know where they used to join together? I didn't come from over there when they parade and go out there to park with that drilling, uniform drilling rank. And you take Shepard Smith. Yeah. He was the head drill man over there. And they come over here, didn't they win the prize from all them other numbers of them art fellas? Yeah.
Didn't they win the prize? That was the Grand Marshal or what?
Drilling. Oh, just a big march. Yeah.
The band played a march. You understand? Well they could drill all right. And the women, Miss Patterson there, she had a gang there, because the women, they were

I've seen some of them got nice now too. Yeah, they had in yellow, no yellow suits out there, Miss Patterson. And I'll tell you, they could drill. I used to play, they used to play with, you reckon, used to play for them all the time.
